# wenchang

> A memory store that AI agents write to on their own judgment. A Python library that gives an agent a virtual filesystem of markdown files in Google Cloud Storage, exposed as seven tools (over MCP or directly) with versioned writes and scope-based write rules. Version 0.1.0, MIT license, Python 3.12+.

wenchang is a library, not a service: there is no CLI, console script, or ready-made server. You write a short server script. It is installed from git; there is no PyPI release. The agent chooses what to remember and where to file it. Files are found through `description` and `aliases` metadata, and there is no content search. wenchang does not authenticate callers: you supply a resolver that maps credentials to an identity. Repository: https://github.com/msiebert/wenchang

## Instructions for AI agents

To install and wire wenchang for your user:

1. Confirm Python 3.12+, a GCP project, and an MCP client that can launch a stdio server (for example Claude Code).
2. Install from git: `pip install "wenchang[mcp] @ git+https://github.com/msiebert/wenchang"`. The `mcp` extra installs `mcp>=2.2,<3`.
3. Ask the user which scopes they need (for example `user`, `project`, `organization`), which are shared, and which roles may write each.
4. Create a GCS bucket and make sure Application Default Credentials can read, create, delete, and list objects in it.
5. Create `server.py` from the Setup page: `PromptSlots` (purpose, scope_guidance, seed_areas), `MemoryStore(GcsStorage(bucket))`, an identity resolver, a `ScopePolicy`, then `wenchang.mcp.build_server(...)` and `server.run("stdio")`. Use `InMemoryStorage` only for trials.
6. Register it: `claude mcp add memory -e KEY=value -- /path/to/python /path/to/server.py`, or add it under `mcpServers` in `.mcp.json`.
7. Verify the server lists seven tools: get_memory_index, read_file, list_prefix, write_file, append_line, replace_fact, delete_file (prefixed with `{tool_prefix}_` if configured). The memory prompt is the server's instructions and the resource `wenchang://memory-prompt`.
8. When using memory: call get_memory_index first each session; pass the version you read as expected_version on every write (null creates); never write to the `system/` area; never store financial account numbers, health diagnoses, or anything indicating the user is a minor.

## Docs

- [Overview](https://msiebert.github.io/wenchang/index.md): what wenchang is, how the index, tools, scopes, and areas work, and what the library does and does not provide
- [Setup](https://msiebert.github.io/wenchang/setup.md): install, GCS bucket, a complete server script, MCP client configuration, seeding curated content
- [Prompts](https://msiebert.github.io/wenchang/prompts.md): the four prompt slots, the fixed prompt sections, product, tool_prefix, and source
- [Authorization](https://msiebert.github.io/wenchang/authorization.md): credentials from the request, identity resolver, scope policy, and a per-user, per-project HTTP example
- [Caching](https://msiebert.github.io/wenchang/caching.md): an optional cache for get_memory_index (IndexCache get/set/ttl, a Redis example, invalidate_index for writers that bypass the cache, staleness and privacy limits)
- [Purge & export](https://msiebert.github.io/wenchang/operations.md): operator-only MemoryStore.purge and export for erasing or handing over one entity (stop writers first, max_passes and PurgeIncompleteError, index cache and GCS soft-delete interactions, raw export and restore)
- [Examples](https://msiebert.github.io/wenchang/usage.md): six scenarios from a novelist's writing assistant (recall, timeline append with a version conflict, correcting a fact, deleting a subplot, read-only house style, refusing an account number) with real tool-call JSON and memory files
- [Reference](https://msiebert.github.io/wenchang/reference.md): path and file format, the seven tools with exact parameters and returns, configuration, error taxonomy, limitations

## Optional

- [Full documentation in one file](https://msiebert.github.io/wenchang/llms-full.txt): all pages concatenated as Markdown
- [Reference adopter](https://github.com/msiebert/wenchang/blob/main/evals/reference_adopter.py): a worked slots, policy, and identity configuration (a different domain from the examples here)
- [Behavioral eval scenarios](https://github.com/msiebert/wenchang/tree/main/evals/scenarios): scripted scenarios that grade the memory prompt against a real agent
- [Architecture](https://github.com/msiebert/wenchang/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md): module map and invariants
- [HTML site](https://msiebert.github.io/wenchang/): the same content for humans
